sourceLines.text: Lovers of architecture no longer have to travel far to see some
of the world’s most famous buildings. Architect Adam Reed
Tucker has recreated fifteen of  them using Lego bricks. The
exhibition is called Lego Architecture: Towering Ambition. It
Pieces of Lego
is  being  shown  at  museums  and  art  galleries  until  early
September.
________________ (See question 3.) Popular with children of all ages around the
world, they are small colourful plastic blocks which let you build anything you
can imagine.
Adam Reed Tucker was a professional architect for ten years. In 2001, he decided
he wanted to do something different. He wanted to express his love for buildings
while deepening his understanding of architecture, engineering and construction.
He chose to use something that most people used as children and so could relate
to, and he has recreated some of the world's most famous buildings.
The buildings in the exhibition include the Empire State Building, the Bank of
China Tower and the Burj Al-Arab. The highlight of the exhibition is the Burj Al-
Khalifa in Dubai, the tallest building in the world. Tucker used more than four
hundred and fifty thousand pieces of Lego to make his version, which is more than
five metres tall.
Tucker does all his work by hand, using only pictures of the buildings. He does
not use computers or drawings to plan them. Visitors to the exhibition can watch
him  create  famous  buildings  brick  by  brick.  While  the  exhibition  is  going  on,
Tucker will be working on his latest work, the White House, which is where the
American president lives.
After walking past Tucker’s models, visitors can create their own works at the
building station. They can make houses, office buildings, stores or factories. They
can then place their models on a large map of a city. As more visitors come, the
Lego city will grow.
To  many  people,  Lego  might  seem  like  a  toy  for  kids.  But  Adam  Reed Tucker
proves that the only limit to what the toy can do is a person’s imagination.

sourceLines.text: Your brain, which you use every second of your life, is very delicate. To keep
itself healthy, it constantly needs to repair itself. And to do  this, it needs good
food, energy, oxygen, and time while you sleep to do all this repair work. Here is
some advice on how to keep your brain healthy.
Diet
For a healthy brain, you need to eat plenty of fresh fruit and vegetables. This is
because your brain needs a steady supply of energy. It can only get this from a
sugar called glucose, which is released from carbohydrates. Glucose is found in
carbohydrates you eat, but it is only useful in certain kinds of carbohydrate. These
include carbohydrates found in types of brown bread, which take time for your
body to absorb, so they release their glucose slowly and steadily. Chocolate and
other sugary snacks are not good for your brain. They release their sugar fast so
your brain becomes very active, and then quickly gets tired, leaving you feeling
less energetic than before. Your brain also needs oxygen. To get this oxygen, you
need a supply of iron in your blood. This iron comes from foods such as red meat
and vegetables.
Do not skip breakfast, especially before an exam. Your brain performs less well if
you have not eaten for hours. Scientists have shown that students' test results are
lower when they have not eaten. Of course, you need to eat the right food. Junk
food does not work. The brain needs the right kind of carbohydrates.
Do not go thirsty. Dehydration affects your brain's performance. Do not drink too
much  water,  though,  especially  if  you  are  about  to  sit  an  exam.  Trips  to  the
bathroom will be a problem.
Your brain needs you to be physically active so it gets the oxygen-rich blood it
needs to work well. Studies show that working your muscles and giving your body
a workout improves your memory, and too little physical activity makes your brain
get old fast. So go running, go swimming or have a game of football!
Sleep
Finally,  possibly  the  easiest  way  to  keep  your  brain  healthy  is  to  have  a  good
night's sleep!

sourceLines.text: The egg in the bottle science experiment is very popular. It is thousands of years
old, and can be used to entertain your children, your students or anyone else you
want to make smile. It also helps us learn about air pressure. The object is to get
an  egg  through  the  rim  of  a  bottle  without  breaking  the  egg.  To  perform  this
experiment, you need a bottle, an egg, a box of matches and some water.
First of all, boil an egg and let it cool. Then, put the egg in the rim of the bottle
so people can see that the egg is too wide to go through. When you have done that,
take the egg back out, and take some matches from the  matchbox. Light four or
five of them and drop them into the bottle. Next, put the egg back onto the rim of
the bottle. The egg is sucked into the bottle and falls to the bottom.
The  scientific  explanation  for  what  happens  is  simple.  When  we  drop  the  lit
matches into the bottle, it heats the molecules of air inside. This makes the air
expand as the molecules move away from each other. They go up and out of the
bottle,  pushing  past  the  egg,  to  escape  the  heat  of  the  fire.  Once  the  fire  is
extinguished, the air cools down again, but the egg in the rim of the bottle stops
air from outside entering the bottle. The air pressure inside the bottle is now lower.
This means the air pressure outside is greater. This creates a force that forces the
egg into the lower pressure bottle. So not only does your audience have fun, they
also learn something about science!
While the usual purpose of this experiment is to learn something in a fun way, we
have also used it in medicine for hundreds of years. The Chinese use it to reduce
back  pain.  What  happens  is  that  a  glass  with  a  burning  candle  is  placed  on  a
patient’s back. This creates a force which pulls blood to where the glass is, which
stops the back pain.

sourceLines.text: Trees are the biggest living things on our planet They are also the oldest living
things. Trees tell us about thousands of years of history. The age of trees makes
them useful for scientific research. The rings inside a tree are very useful because
they tell scientists about changes in the climate thousands of years ago.
The oldest living thing on earth is Great Oakie, a tree which grows in the USA. It
is about 4,700 years old, which means it was already growing when the Egyptians
built the Pyramids. Sri Maha Bodhi is a tree in Sri Lanka. It is the oldest tree in
the world that has a recorded history, of more than 23 centuries.
The gingko tree is one of the oldest types of tree. We know that it was living 160
million years ago when there were dinosaurs. But gingko fossils disappeared about
7 million years ago. Scientists thought that it was extinct until it was found in
Japan in 1691. Today, it is popular in parks and gardens and is used in medicine.
Trees can teach us about how working together can help us. Scientists are only
just beginning to understand how it all works, but we now know that groups of
trees share their resources. Strong trees share food and water with weaker trees.
They do this through their roots and through the soil.
Many people believe that trees are good for people as well. Patients in hospital
get better faster and go home quicker if there are trees outside their rooms. Not
only that. Trees take more energy from the sun than any other living thing. Some
people believe that you feel this energy when you put your arms around a tree
and hug it. If you go to a park in Britain, you might see somebody hugging a tree
like  it  was  a  person.  These  people  are  sometimes  called  tree-huggers,  and  the
activity is called tree-hugging.
Tree-huggers believe that tree-hugging helps you relax, makes you sleep better,
and help you to feel better. And more and more people are doing it. The politician
Gerry Adams recently told a journalist that he hugged trees. He said that it stopped
him feeling nervous. Trees are essential for the environment and our planet.

sourceLines.text: Great But There Are Risks
The Internet is one of the wonders of the modern age. Within just the last twenty
years,  it  has  transformed  our  lives,  changing  the  way  we  shop,  learn  about  the
world and spend free time. However, like a beautiful city with risky areas, it has
its threats. Here is a brief description of some of those threats, and advice on what
you can do to avoid them.
Some People Want To Snoop On You
The most common danger is that of spyware, software which, as its name suggests,
exists to record without your knowledge which websites you visit, your passwords
and even your credit card details, then passes it on to a third party. There are many
ways  your  computer  can  become  infected  with  spyware,  but  the  most  common
include downloading music or movies illegally, and opening email attachments.
Some People Want To Harm You
Next, there is malware. Short for malicious software, malware does exactly as its
name suggests, existing just to hurt you. It includes viruses that shut down your
system, programs that destroy your data, and software that sends unwanted emails
to everybody in your email address book, which can be very upsetting.
Some People Want To Rob You
Finally, there is phishing, the practice of sending spam email in an attempt to trick
Internet users into giving up personal information such as their credit card or bank
account  details.  Phishing  most  often  comes  as  emails  claiming to  be  from  your
bank. Typically, the emails claim that, unless you reply with your personal banking
information, your account will be closed. Those who reply to such emails often
find that their credit card bill rockets astronomically as a result. In this situation,
credit card companies are not helpful at all, and might take your card from you.
Keep Them Out
So how can you keep safe on the Internet? Firstly, make sure you have a firewall
installed.  A  firewall  is  an  application  that  monitors  traffic  in  and  out  of  your
Internet  connection.  Viruses,  malware  and  software  can  all  be  controlled  by  a
firewall.  It  is  your  first  line  of  defence.  Most  modern  computers  come  with  a
firewall as standard, for example, Windows Firewall. However, if you want greater
protection,  there  is  a  range  of  free  or  paid-for  firewalls  available  to  download
online.
Find Them If They Get In
Next, there’s antivirus software. One of your computer’s most important defences,
it runs continuously in the background scanning for threats. If you have a relatively
new computer, it probably already has antivirus protection. If not, Symantec and
Mcafee are well-known and well-respected brands.
Finally, there is email phishing. Here, your best defence is common sense. Your
bank or credit card company will not send you emails threatening to close your
account. After all, they only want your money. The next time you get an email like
this, delete it straight away.
Enjoy Yourself But Be Safe
So enjoy the Internet. Explore it, as you would a beautiful city. Just be aware that
it has its dangers, but as long as you follow the simple advice given above, you
will be safe. For more information, visit our website at www.getsafeonline.org .uk

sourceLines.text: Road transport is one of the biggest sources of pollution in the UK, contributing
to  climate  change,  poor  air  quality,  congestion  and  noise.  Of  the  33  million
vehicles  on  our  roads,  27  million  are  cars.  Here  are  the  kinds  of  pollution  or
problems which cars contribute to, followed by ways in which you can help solve
these problems.
Road transport accounts for 22% of total UK emissions of carbon dioxide (CO 2),
the major contributor to climate change. As traffic levels are predicted to increase,
road transport will continue to add to greenhouse gas emissions.
Air Quality
Air  pollutants  from  transport  include  carbon  monoxide  and  other  damaging
substances.  All  have  a  negative  impact  on  the  health  of  people,  animals  and
vegetation. Air quality in the UK is improving, but  many areas still  have high
levels of air pollution. In town centres and on busy roads, vehicles are responsible
for  most  pollution.  Although  new  technology  and  cleaner  fuel  will  continue  to
reduce emissions, the increasing number of vehicles is reducing these benefits.
Noise
Noise from traffic affects 30% of people in the UK. Sources include engine noise,
tyre noise, car horns, car stereos, door slamming, and brakes. The sound of engines
is a problem in towns and cities, while in rural areas tyre noise on busy roads is
the main source of noise.
Resource Use
Vehicles have a major impact on the environment through their construction, use
and eventual disposal. It is estimated that of the CO 2 emissions produced over a
car's lifespan 10% comes from its manufacture and 5% from its disposal, with the
remaining 85% coming from its use.
While travel by car is often the only practical option, there are steps we can all
take to reduce the number of journeys we take and their impact on the environment.
Follow these suggestions to minimise your impact:
1) Avoid using cars for short journeys: walk, cycle, or take a bus.
2) Do maintenance: check tyre pressure and brakes to reduce fuel consumption.
3) Lighten up : don’t consume fuel by carrying unnecessary loads.
4) Drive gently: racing starts and sudden stops increase fuel consumption.
5) Reduce  your  speed:  at  around  80  kph  emissions  will  be  lowest,  rising
dramatically above 110 kph.
6) Switch off when not moving: do not use the engine unnecessarily
7) Think about those around you : reduce the volume of your car stereo.
8) Air conditioning increases fuel consumption: only use it when necessary.
9) Share journeys: travel with friends or neighbours.
10) Buy a car that uses less fuel.
For more information, visit our website at www.environmentalprotection.org.uk

sourceLines.text: Nowadays, most people and workplaces cannot function without a computer, so it
is surprising that technology is not used more often in schools. The reasons for its
use  in  the  classroom  are  well-known.  Firstly,  computers  are  very  popular.
Secondly, having more computers in the classroom could raise teaching standards
and  address problems in schools. It is clear that we  should use computers in the
classroom. This article examines not only reasons why we should, but also some of
the problems.
Exploration
Computers  allow  students  to  learn  using  the  Internet.  Using  the  Internet  to  do
research,  which is often more stimulating than using paper encyclopaedias to do
research, can keep students  engaged in learning longer.  However, some students
might  be distracted by other sites  or activities they find on the Internet. While
students should be doing research on Wikipedia, some might waste time checking
their facebook account.
Lesson Integration
Incorporating  technology  into  lessons can  make  sure  that  students  are  engaged
instead  of  losing  interest.  Normally  boring  lessons  such  as  Study  Skills  can  be
made  more  engaging  with  YouTube  videos  and  other  interactive  media.  On  the
other hand, finding the right materials online is not easy. It can sometimes be very
difficult.  Teachers  may  spend  more  time  planning  lessons,  becoming  tired  and
angry.

especially  laptops  for  student  use,  has  to be  replaced  every  two  to three  years.
Technicians are required for schools with classroom technology,  which makes it
necessary to spend even more money on employing them. The  more  technology
schools use, the more staff it is necessary to employ in order to keep it running.

The  training  required  for  teachers  and  students  to  be  able  to  use  classroom
technology is an advantage. They can use this training in part-time jobs and their
future  careers.  The  disadvantage  is  that  this  training  can  be  costly  and  time-
consuming, and many teachers do not want to participate. Some teachers may feel
that they already have enough skills. Others may not be able to learn as quickly as
their students.
Teacher Tools
Technology in the classroom is not just for students. Teachers can use technology
to keep student records, plan lessons and communicate with parents.

sourceLines.text: If you look down at our planet from space, most of what you see is water. 70% of
the planet is covered by ocean, with only 30% of our  globe consisting of land.
This is why the Earth is sometimes called the Water Planet.
Beneath  the  surface  of  all  that  water  lie  mountains,  volcanoes  and  almost
bottomless  trenches.  In  the  oceans,  there  are  mountain  ranges  greater  than  the
Himalayas or the Andes, and single mountains called seamounts. There are ocean
trenches,  which  are  the  deepest  parts  of  the  oceans.  There  are  valleys  where
earthquakes and volcanic eruptions are common, causing volcanoes to rise above
the water’s surface as islands.
When studying the composition of these geological features, oceanographers have
discovered that rocks on the ocean bottom are much younger than similar rocks
found on land. The rock brought back by deep-sea drilling ships varies greatly in
age, but nothing from the ocean floor is more than about 200 million years old.
This makes ocean rock very young compared with the continents, which contain
rocks of up to about 4 billion years old.
Where does all this information come from? Oceanographers know what there is
on the ocean floor because it has been mapped. To make maps of the ocean floor,
the depth of the ocean must be known in many places. In the early days of ocean
exploration, sailors used a long piece of rope, with a heavy weight at one end. The
depth was measured by dropping the weight into the water and finding when the
weight  reached  the  bottom.  Today's  oceanographers,  however,  use  sonar
instruments. Today, most depth measurements are made using an echo sounder.
Instead of dropping a weight, sound energy is sent towards the bottom of the sea.
By measuring the journey time of the sound waves, the depth of the water can be
measured.

sourceLines.text: Why, Where and When They Occur
Tropical cyclones, also known as typhoons and hurricanes, are caused by the heat
released when warm humid air rises from the sea. The time of year, therefore,
when tropical cyclones are most likely to occur (often called Hurricane Season)
is when the sea is at its warmest. For the Northern Hemisphere (including the
Caribbean and South East Asia) this is from June to November. For the Southern
Hemisphere (including East Africa) this is from November to April. You should
consider avoiding travel to these regions during these periods.
Tropical cyclones lose strength as they reach the coast and begin to move over
land.  Inland  areas are  generally free  from  danger of  tropical  hurricanes.
However, the route that a tropical cyclone takes remains very difficult to predict.
The margin of error just 24 hours before the arrival of a tropical cyclone can be
as much as 50 miles.
What You Should Do If There Is A Tropical Cyclone
It is advisable to follow local advice, which in some cases will be to leave the
area immediately if a tropical cyclone is heading your way.
If you are in a cyclone region during Hurricane Season:
1) regularly check country travel advice
2) monitor local radio, TV and press
3) keep in touch with your travel or tour company
4) register with your local embassy
5) follow local advice
6) remember that airports and hotels may shut down if a hurricane approaches
How Much Help We Can Give
Tropical cyclones can seriously damage a country’s infrastructure. It may take
time for airports, roads or hospitals to reopen, and there may be serious shortages
of accommodation, food, water and health facilities.
Our  ability  to  help  our  nationals  may  be  limited  (perhaps  seriously)  in  these
circumstances. We do not have embassies in every country likely to be affected
by  tropical  cyclones,  for  example,  on  some  islands  in  the  Caribbean.  This  is
likely to have an impact on the level of help we can provide in certain places.
The Effects Of A Tropical Cyclone
Tropical cyclones can cause damage in a number of ways:
1) high  winds:  buildings  can  be  destroyed  or  damaged;  trees,  power  and
telephone lines toppled
2) storm  surge:  a  hurricane  can  provoke  a  temporary  rise  in  sea  level  of
several metres which can flood coastal areas and damage buildings on the
shoreline
3) very heavy rainfall: this can cause local or widespread flooding
For more information, visit our website at www.ministryoftravel.gov

sourceLines.text: Mobile phones have had an important effect on our lives and the way that we do
everyday tasks. Many of these changes are clear while there are others we may
not even know about.
Mobiles have brought a new meaning to the term multitasking. Twenty years ago,
it was not possible to talk to the office while out shopping, or have a three-way
conference while making dinner. Mobile phones have enabled us to do various
tasks all at the same time.
________________ (See question 3.) Children can contact you if they miss their
ride home, and your wife can phone if she is going to be late home from the mall.
If you have teenage children, they can call to ask permission to go somewhere,
and, with GPS features, you can check where they are.
We  do  not  notice  many  of  these  advantages.  Have  you  ever  arrived  at  the
supermarket and realised you have forgotten your shopping list? The first thing
you do is to call home and ask what to buy. In the past, you had to drive home to
get it. If your car breaks down on the motorway, you call for assistance from the
emergency services from the comfort of your car instead of having to walk to a
pay phone. Mobile phones have made our lives much more convenient.
Mobile phones have also changed the way that people interact with each other.
When we call someone, we call a person and not a place. Unlike when you phone
a landline, someone is always home. Mobile phones also enable us to call if we
are going to be late for a meeting, although this means mobile users often run
late. Many mobile users seem to think that appointment times are not  concrete.
They often use their mobile phones to rearrange their arrival time.
One of the negative effects of the mobile is that we do not talk to strangers any
more.  For  example,  in  the  past,  people  waiting  for  a  bus  would  have  a
conversation while waiting. People might develop friendships along their routes.
This no longer happens. Today when people wait for a bus, they just pull out their
mobile phones and speak with friends. In large cities, many people do not know
their neighbours, even though they may have lived in the same place for years.
As a result of mobile phones, our society is losing the face-to-face interaction
that was an important part of life in the past.
Mobile phones are a great help in everyday life. You should remember, however,
to put it away once in a while and pay attention to the world around you.

sourceLines.text: The Rise in Food Miles
Long-distance  food  transport  is  nothing  new.  Food  has  been  traded  between
nations for centuries. These days, however, food travels further than ever before.
Ninety-five per cent of the fruit and half of the vegetables in Britain are imported.
The amount of food being flown into Britain doubled in the 1990s and is predicted
to rise further each year. And British fish is now sent to China (where labour costs
are much lower) for processing, and then sent back.
Firstly, we are now able to fly in seasonal food all year round. Secondly, these
days we prefer to buy more processed food (which is more likely to be imported).
Finally, we can now afford it. Today we do not just import a few delicacies to
supplement local produce. We transport huge volumes of food around our road
networks, and, from other continents, import out-of-season produce.
Long-distance  food  transportation  involves  lorries  and  aeroplanes,  which use  a
great deal of fuel. As a result, many tonnes of CO2 are emitted, which contributes
to global warming. That, however, is just the starting point. Other reasons include
wanting  to  eat  fresher  food,  supporting  local  producers  and  the  economy,  and

and avoid air-freighted foods. Another effective way to achieve a low carbon diet
is to cut down on meat and dairy products. This will help you  minimise waste
through cooking the right amount of food.
What Kind of Food?
Cook fresh, seasonal food bought that day. Buying organic food can also help.
Organic farming can cut down on the fossil fuels used in its transport, but it is
important to buy locally grown organic food rather than imported. To give an idea
of how far imported organic food travels, a typical basket of 26 imported organic
foods may have travelled the distance of six times around the equator: 250,000

for a university place for their child, saying that a great mind could be lost if he
is not given a chance to study at university.
Bob Smith, the son of a British father and a Spanish mother, passed a high school
chemistry exam at the age of six.
The case of the child genius, whose parents claim he could walk at six months and
construct complex sentences by his first birthday, has caused both curiosity and
concern. Experts believe that the lack of a normal childhood can do serious long-
term psychological damage.
Yesterday, Bob’s father, Ken Smith, said that it had been clear from birth that his
son was very unusual. “As a toddler,” said Mr Smith, “he would seek out science
books in the library, preferring texts with complicated scientific illustrations. He
would absorb these and comment on them later. By the time he was three, he was
interested  in  hyper-dimensional  shapes  and  would  draw  their  shadows  in  two
dimensions as a game.”
Mr Smith also said that his son showed an interest in chemistry when he was six.
Once, he found a high school chemistry exam at his aunt’s house. “He got all the
questions right. It turned out that he had taught himself chemistry on the internet,”
he said.
He denied that child prodigies usually failed at university and said that it would
be unfair to allow his son’s mind to stagnate. “Imagine you are the strongest man
in the world and someone says to you, try lifting something small like a banana.
It’s  like  asking  him  to  deny  his  true  nature.  Well,  it’s  the  same  with  a  child
prodigy,” he said.
The parents are looking for a sponsor for their child’s university education and
say  that  one  of them  would accompany  him  during  his  studies.  Mrs  Smith,  his
mother, denied they put pressure on him. “He is home-schooled most of the time,
but he goes to school for computer classes and has friends there,” she said.
Mr Smith added, “You have never seen anyone more relaxed and laidback in your
life.” The couple said that it was too early to tell if their other sons, Eric, 4, and
Norman, 1, were equally gifted.

that  the  child  was  a  chemistry  prodigy.  “Clearly,  a  normal  school  would  be
incredibly  frustrating  for  Bob,”  he  said.  He  added  that  his  own  university  had

sourceLines.text: Piracy and pirates have existed since ancient times, when they attacked the trading
routes of Ancient Greece, and stole the cargo of Roman trading ships. In some
parts of the world, piracy exists today, for example in the South China Seas and
along  the  coast  of  Africa.  However,  the  Golden  Age  of  Piracy,  centred  in  the
Caribbean, lasted from about 1650 to 1720, a period which has given us famous
names such as Blackbeard and Captain Kidd. Let’s take a look at that place and
period, and find out what eventually happened to its pirates.
When Christopher Columbus discovered America at the end of the 15th century,
these new lands were soon found to be a rich source of silver and gold. From the
16th century, large Spanish ships began to sail to Europe carrying this silver and
gold, cargoes that pirates found impossible to resist. Thieves and robbers came to
the  Caribbean from all over the  world to become  pirates. Ever since  then, the
Caribbean has been famous for piracy.
Why Were These Pirates So Successful?
Their ships usually carried far more  crew than ordinary ships. This meant they
outnumbered their victims, and stories about the violence and cruelty of pirates
meant that they had a terrifying reputation. They advertised this with their flag:
the Skull and Crossbones. All these things together meant that victims often gave
in without a shot fired.
The  most  valuable  prizes  were  boxes  of  gold,  silver  and  jewels.  Coins  were
especially popular because pirate crews could share them out easily. These coins
were far more likely to be made of silver than gold, because ten times more silver
than gold was mined in America. However, pirates did not only seize precious
cargoes like these. They also wanted things they could use, such as food, barrels
of water, sails, anchors for when they didn’t want their ship to move away, and
other equipment for their ship, and instruments such as those belonging to the
ship's doctor.
Successful  pirate  attacks  became  so  frequent  and  dangerous  that  governments
were forced to take action. In the 18th century, they sent heavily armed and fast-
moving  frigates to the pirates' favourite hunting grounds. Terrible battles were
fought, during which some of the most famous pirates such as Blackbeard were
killed. Other pirates were captured and put on trial, and were executed in public.
The Golden Age of Piracy was over.

sourceLines.text: On the outside, Ken was a typical student. Living away from home was expensive
and he owed money. Like most students, he had a computer and a phone in his
room, but instead of using them to study, he turned them into the tools of a 21st
century criminal.
In his short career as a fraudster, Ken, who is trying to rebuild his life after serving
a  long  prison  sentence,  estimates  that,  online,  he  stole  as  much  as  £250,000
through stolen credit card details, identity theft and bank account takeover. For
Ken,  who  went  to  prison  for  four  years,  the  chance  to  use  people’s  ignorance
against them was too easy. “Maybe it took an hour a night if I really felt like it.
But to me it felt like a bit of fun and a pastime which developed into an easy way
of making money.” he said.
In spare moments around his university schedule (he was a law student), this young
man would get card details taken from websites or from other criminals. Later, he
would go on spending sprees that got him cars, clothes and cash.
“It was just a game to see how far you could go,” he said. “My favourite trick was
to get a card in someone’s name and use it. Then, within 24 hours, you call the
bank up and convince them that you are the genuine person and that you haven’t
made those transactions, and they refund it. Then you just go to the cash machine
and take it all out again.” He even sent flowers to one victim, using their stolen
bank details to pay for the bouquet.
Statistics from CIFAS, the UK’s fraud prevention service, show that identity theft
was up almost 20% last year, while Internet and card fraud rose to an all-time high
Martin Gill is a  criminologist at the University of Leicester. He has studied the
actions  and  motivations  of  fraudsters  and  Ken  was  one  of  the  people  he
interviewed. Gill believes that fraudsters think that online crime is easy. “One of
the things that comes through is the belief that they’re not going to get caught,”

sourceLines.text: Far from being a trader who spent years in China, he probably never went further
than  Rome,  according  to  a  team  of  archaeologists.  They  suspect  the  adventurer
picked up stories about China from sailors. He then put the stories in a book which
he claimed to be an account of his travels between 1271 and 1291.  It details his
friendship with Kublai Khan, the Chinese ruler.
But now a team of Italian archaeologists have cast doubts on his story. Professor
Daniele  Petrella  of  Naples  University  told  history  magazine  Focus  Storia  there
were many mistakes in Marco Polo’s description of Kublai Khan’s invasions of
Japan in 1274 and 1281. ‘He confuses the two, mixing up details about the first
expedition with those of the second,’ Professor Petrella said.
In his account of the first invasion, he describes the fleet leaving Korea and being
hit by a typhoon before it reached the Japanese coast,' said Professor Petrella. 'But
that happened in 1281. Is it really possible that he could confuse events which were
seven years apart?'
Polo’s description of the Mongol fleet did not square with the design of the ships
the archaeologists found in Japan, as he had written of ships with five masts, while
those found had only three.
‘It was during our dig in Japan that doubts began to emerge about what he wrote,’
added Professor Petrella. 'When he describes Kublai Khan’s fleet he talks about
the paint that was used on the ships. He used the word chunam, which is not a word
in Chinese. In fact, it is the Persian word for paint. It’s strange that instead of
using local names to describe places, he used Persian names.'
The explorer claimed to have worked for Kublai Khan, but his name does not appear
in any Chinese records.
The latest claims  back those made in a book by British academic Frances Wood
entitled Did Marco Polo go to China?  She argued he never went beyond Rome and
that his famous account is a collection of lies.

sourceLines.text: Have you ever looked out from a plane flying at 30,000 feet to see the vast expanse
of  empty  ocean  and  uninhabited  land,  and  wondered  how  people  can  have  any
effect on the Earth? I certainly have, but it is now clear that we are causing a great
deal  of  damage  to  the  natural  environment.  And  the  planes  which  take  us  to
destinations around the globe contribute to our biggest environmental  problem:
Global Warming.
________________  (See  question  3).  There  are  a  huge  number  of  fascinating
places to explore and the cost of air transport has decreased rapidly over the years.
Many people can fly around the world for little more than  the contents of their
weekly pay packet.
Unfortunately, planes produce far more carbon dioxide (CO 2) than any other form
of  public  transport.  CO 2 is  a  greenhouse  gas,  which  traps  the  heat  of  the  Sun,
preventing it from leaving our atmosphere, and causing the Earth’s temperature to
rise. Scientists predict that in the near future the climate in Britain will resemble
that of the Mediterranean. If Global Warming continues, many tourist destinations
such as the Maldives will disappear because of rising sea levels.
So  what  can  be  done  to  solve  the  problem?  Well,  although  aircraft  engine
manufacturers are making more fuel-efficient engines and researching alternative
fuels,  it  will  be  decades  before  air  travel  is  not  damaging  to  the  environment.
Because  governments  do  not  seem  to  take  the  problem  seriously,  it  is  up  to
individual travellers to do what they can to help.
The most obvious way of dealing with the problem is to not travel by plane at all.
Environmental groups like Friends of the Earth encourage people to travel by train
and plan holidays in their own country. However, with prices of flights at an all
time low, and exotic destinations more popular than ever, it is hard to persuade
British  tourists  to  choose  Blackpool  instead  of  Bangkok,  or  Morecambe over
Malaysia.
However,  there  is  a  way  of  offsetting  the  carbon  dioxide  we  produce  when  we
travel  by  plane.  A  company  called  Future  Forests  can  do  this  for  you.  They
calculate the amount of CO 2 you are responsible for producing on your flight, and
plant the number of trees which will absorb this CO 2. Another company does the
same,  and  also  invests  money  in  energy  saving  projects  such  as  efficient  light
bulbs for villagers in Mauritius.

sourceLines.text: According to a major study of global illness, air pollution has become the world's
fastest growing cause of death. Despite recent improvements in healthcare, the
areas  most  seriously  affected  are  the  fast-growing  cities  of  South-East  Asia,
which  have  become  world  centres  for global  air pollution.  This  is  largely  the
result of an explosion in car use.
In  2010,  more  than  2.1  million  people  in  Asia  died  prematurely  from  air
pollution, often from the gasses emitted from cars and lorries. Other major causes
of air pollution include construction and industry. Of these deaths, says the study,
1.2 million were in East Asia and China, and 712,000 in South Asia, including
India.
Worldwide, a record 3.2 million people died from air pollution in 2010, compared
with 800,000 in 2000. It now ranks for the first time in the world's Top Ten List
of Killer Diseases, says the study.
These unexpected figures have given scientists a very unpleasant surprise. David
Pettit, director of Global Air Programme, says, ‘That's a terribly high number,
and many more people than previously thought. Earlier studies were limited to
data only from urban areas like Tokyo and Shanghai.’
Eric Smith, head of air pollution at the Centre for Science and Environment, a
New Delhi-based environmental group, says, ‘There is hard evidence now of the
dangers to all of air pollution, and this is why we have to act immediately to
reduce the health risks, particularly for children, elderly and the poor. No-one
can escape toxic air.’
________________ (See question 8.) The full effects of air pollution on health
in  Asia  will  only  be  seen  in  the  future,  he  says.  ‘Toxic  effects  like  cancer
sometimes  appear  only  after  a  very  long  period.  Therefore,  exposure  to  air
pollution will have to be reduced today to reduce the future level of disease,’ he
says.
According to the report, which was produced by different universities working
in  conjunction  with  the  UN,  65%  of  all  air  pollution  deaths  are  now  in  Asia,
which  lost  52  million  years  of  healthy  life  from  air  pollution  in  2010.  Air
pollution  also  contributes  to  higher  rates  of  mental  illness,  strokes  and  heart
attacks.
If the figures for outdoor air pollution were combined with those of indoor air
pollution,  caused  largely  by  people  cooking  indoors  with  wood,  air  pollution
would  now  be  the  second  highest  killer  in  the  world,  behind  only  high  blood
pressure.

sourceLines.text: Phishing email messages are designed to steal your personal information. These
fraudulent email messages send you to websites and phone numbers where you
are asked for this data. This is done so phishers can steal money from you. This
webpage gives a few simple clues to help spot these fake messages so you stay
safe online.
These messages take a number of forms:
They appear to come from a bank or a social networking site. 
 They appear to be from someone in your email address book.
 They include official-looking logos taken from legitimate websites.
 They ask you to call a number where an  automated audio response unit
takes your personal data.
To make these phishing email messages look real, phishers use images that come
from legitimate websites. However, you are taken not to the legitimate website,
but to a phony site that looks exactly like the official site.
Here are some phrases commonly used in phishing emails.
Verify your account.
________________ (See question 6.). If you receive an email claiming to come
from Microsoft or another well-known business asking you to update credit card
information or a password, do not respond. This is a phishing scam.
You have won the lottery.
The lottery scam is a common scam known as Advanced Fee Fraud. One common
form of Advanced Fee Fraud is a message that claims you have won a large sum
of money.
If you don't respond within 48 hours, your account will be closed.
These messages try to panic you so you respond without thinking. A phishing
email  message  might  also  claim  that  your  response  is  required  because  your
account has been compromised.
Sometimes phishing email messages direct you to fake websites. They can contain
forms that you fill out like you would a form on a legitimate website. Phishing
links  may  contain  a  real  company's  name,  but  they  are  usually  masked .  This
means the link does not take you to that address but somewhere different, usually
a fake website.
Cybercriminals also use web addresses that  resemble the names of well-known
companies. For  example,  the  address  www.microsoft.com could appear  instead
as:
 www.micosoft.com
www.mircosoft.com 
www.verify-microsoft.com 
This is called typo-squatting or cybersquatting.
For more information, click Email and web scams: How to help protect yourself.

sourceLines.text: The RMS Titanic was a passenger liner that became famous for its collision with
an iceberg and sinking in 1912. Built at the Harland and Wolff shipyard in Belfast,
Ireland, the Titanic was the largest liner in the world at the time of her sinking.
During the Titanic's first journey (from Southampton to New York), she struck an
iceberg at 11:40 PM on Sunday April 14, 1912, broke into two pieces, and sank
two hours and forty minutes later at 2:20 AM on Monday April 15.
________________  (See  question  4.)  The  ship  offered  a  swimming  pool,
gymnasium, a Turkish bath, library and squash court. First-class accommodation
was decorated with wood and expensive furniture. In addition, the Café Parisienne
offered superb food for the first-class passengers. Second-class and even third-
class accommodation was considered as good as first-class on many other ships of
the day. The ship offered three lifts for first-class passengers and offered one lift
for second-class passengers.
According  to  the  United  States  Senate  investigation,  1,523  people  died  in  the
accident, making it one of the worst disasters in history and by far the most famous.
The Titanic's design used some of the most advanced technology available at the
time and the ship was believed to be "unsinkable." It was a terrible shock that,
despite the advanced technology and experienced crew, the Titanic sank with a
great  loss  of  life.  The  newspaper  interest  in  the  Titanic's  famous  victims,  the
legends about what happened on board the ship, the resulting changes to sea law,
and  the  discovery  of  the  wreck  on  1  September  1985  by  a  team  led  by  Robert
Ballard and Jean-Louis Michel have made the Titanic famous in the years since.
As news of the disaster spread, many people were shocked that the Titanic could
sink  with  such  great  loss  of  life  despite  all  of  its  technological  advances.
Newspapers  were  filled  with  stories  and  descriptions  of  the  disaster.  Many
organisations were set up to help the victims and their families, many of whom
lost their only breadwinner, or, in the case of third-class survivors, lost everything
they owned. The people of the city of Southampton were deeply affected by the
sinking. According to the  Hampshire Chronicle on April 20, 1912, almost 1,000
local families were directly affected. Almost every street in the Chapel district lost
more than one resident and over 500 households lost a member.

sourceLines.text: Diabetes is a long-term condition caused by too much glucose, a type of sugar, in
the  blood.  There  are  two  main  types  of  diabetes,  type  1  diabetes  and  type  2
diabetes.  In the UK, diabetes affects approximately 2.8 million people. More than
two and a half million people are thought to have type 2 diabetes. There is no cure.
For more information, including causes, symptoms and treatment of diabetes, click
the link for the Health A-Z topic on type 2 diabetes.
What are the symptoms?
The main symptoms of diabetes are:
1) feeling very thirsty
2) going to the toilet a lot, especially at night
3) tiredness
4) weight loss
Symptoms of type 1 diabetes can develop quickly, over weeks or even days. Many
people have type 2 diabetes for years without knowing it because early symptoms
can be general.
How does diabetes occur?
Normally,  the  amount  of  sugar  in  the  blood  is  controlled  by  a  chemical  called
insulin. When food is digested and enters your bloodstream, insulin moves any
glucose  out  of  the  blood  and  into  cells,  where  it  is  used  to  produce  energy.
However, in people with diabetes, the body is unable to turn glucose into energy.
What is type 1 diabetes?
Type 1 diabetes occurs when the body produces no insulin. It usually develops
before the age of 40, often during the teenage years, which is why it is sometimes
called early-onset diabetes (type 2 diabetes more commonly affects older people).
Type 1 diabetes is far less common than type 2 diabetes, which occurs when the
body  produces too  little  insulin  or  when  the  body  does  not  react  properly  to
insulin. People with type 1 diabetes make up only 10% of all people with diabetes.
If you have type 1 diabetes, you will need to take insulin injections for life. You
must  also  make  sure  that  your  blood  glucose  levels  stay  balanced  by  avoiding
unhealthy food and eating plenty of fruit and vegetables.
What is type 2 diabetes?
Type 2 diabetes occurs when not enough insulin is produced by the body for it to
function properly. Sometimes, the body does not react to insulin.  This is called
insulin resistance. Type 2 diabetes is far more common than type 1 diabetes, which
occurs when the body does not produce any insulin at all. Around 90% of all adults
in the UK with diabetes have type 2 diabetes.
